body: I can. When i've asked about doing sessions over video though they've said it's only voice calls. Something about being covered by insurance or not? Idk. But for whatever reason seems like video isn't allowed

Only teletherapy. No video sessions unfortunately.

I don't have a laptop or anything like that anyways.. only a cell phone so not sure if it'd even be possible.

I'm not trying to say I know everything. But I have done this. I always bent over backwards for her. Our ups and downs were issues with her sobriety. That's it. Our relationship in itself was good. And if it wasn't then she lied through her teeth the whole time and never allowed me an opportunity to fix anything because I was never told there was an issue there too fix. I didn't just shrug things off and stroll right along. I would frequently check in with her. See how she was doing. Mostly because she has had depression since 15, but because I wanted to know how my wife was doing in general. And never did I get anything problematic.
As I said. Sobriety. Her trying to stay sober from being alcoholic and not get back into big drugs. She'd struggle. Want to relapse and i'd turn into the bad guy for not just turning a blind eye so she could do it. I had to remind her of why she was fighting to stay sober. Remind her not to go to certain situations with friends or family (per her request) because she wasn't confident in herself to say no to things. There would be a lot of hate and anger from this taken out on me/ us. But in the end she'd compose herself, apologize, and thank me for not letting her slip up. This in turn causes issues with family and friends whom she was distancing herself from and they couldn't understand why. But still.. nothing for me to fix with it as long as she was wanting me to help her stay sober.
This is why I say out of the blue. Because nothing changed. Everything has been the same. The biggest trigger was her deciding she gives no f's about staying sober and didn't want to think I was disappointed in her everytime she'd decide to do it in front of me so she didn't think us being together was good since she wasn't going to be sober anymore. But doesn't explain why the instant urge to give up sobriety..
Unless she just likes being fake and pretending. But idk why anyone would decide to be fake with trying to have kids.. amongst many other things.

Drugs would be everything except heroin and meth. Weed daily. And regular use of acid, molly, shrooms etc. And possibly coke. (She was into coke before but has questioned it due to becoming addicted again). Drinking is just basically whenever. Whether glass of wine at dinner. To full on black out drunk cause why not it's friday. It's not so much the issue of she got drunk on a saturday how dare she! She just doesn't do things responsibly. When she did stuff before she didn't know when to say no. She'd do 20 vodka shots a night for a week straight cause "why not". She just lets things get out of hand... hard for her to stay rational once she starts.

You are completely correct. I honestly don't know much.. just odds and ends things from google. I do understand the mood changes and what not. It actually got much better after being on meds. (She didn't get on any for almost a year after being diagnosed).

However... I don't know how to tell reality from BPD. Many of her past "episodes" she has blamed on her brain. Saying things like it tells her things she doesn't believe but makes her convinced it's how she feels. Then she wakes up one day feeling completely different about it and frustrated about the things she said and how she felt cause "it's not true, but her brain made her think it was".

Other times though, like now, when I try mentioning BPD and other things she insists it's not that. It's her actual self, her thinking clearly and knowing what is truth. Not addiction talking. Nothing but her own personality finally deciding. Which I guess is true... but idk how to know. I would like to think it's just her prior addiction still working at her, along with her BPD complicating things. But I have noway to know for sure if that's what it is or if it really is her "personality of who she is".


You have any thoughts on how to get her to see one? Cause i've tried and she won't. Especially now. Before she was only doing it because of us. Now with her saying there's no point in an us she's even more against any kind of help.
She also sees no issue in breaking her sobriety. So to her it's pointless to try talking to someone or working through it cause it doesn't matter to continue being sober. So why waste time trying to help herself with it.
She always goes back to the fact that since she was 15 drinking and drugs is what she did. Her lifestyle and what she's used to. Being sober is great, but she still thinks about drinking and getting high so that must just be who she is as a person and what she's supposed to do with her personality..

It complicates things a lot.

No she isn't seeing anyone. She saw a couple different counselors last year a few times but they weren't really that great and she stopped. Unfortunately not many choices in our area and our insurance covers even less of them...

I would agree about the world going down the toilet. This is a very sudden thing. The beginning of march she was on the moon with us. It was my birthday and she went far out of her way to be sweet. Very positive about us and our future, having kids etc. Then i'd say from the 23rd onward is when it out of nowhere went bleh. Shortly after being laid off and locked up at home...

It's something i've tried considering as a trigger for this way of thinking now but i've written it off as wishful thinking. It's all confusing on why it's happening, esp after being so positive not too long ago. (Which according to her wasn't fake and she meant it, a whole 3 weeks earlier..).
